quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #4
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Trucks under 18,000 lbs. are allowed.
A hill is ahead.
A truck stop is ahead.
No trucks are allowed.

questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Stop.
No U-turn.
Yield.
Do not enter.

questions.explanation: This sign is placed at the start of one-way streets and ramps. It tells you not to drive in the direction you are heading.

questions.question: Can you drive around or under a gate that is moving at a railroad crossing?

options.text: Yes, if a train is not too close.
Yes, if your vehicle will not damage the gate.
Yes, if you look both ways carefully.
No, never.

questions.explanation: Flashing red lights, lowered gates, and bells at a railroad crossing mean you must stop completely. Do not cross until the lights and bells stop and the gates are fully up. Never drive around or under a moving gate.

questions.question: Must you obey school crossing guards?

options.text: Yes, always.
Only during school hours.
Only if you see children.

questions.explanation: Always obey crossing guards near schools. Watch for them and follow their directions.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The road is getting wider.
The right lane is ending soon. Move left.
A highway entrance ramp is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The right lane is ending soon. Move left.
questions.explanation: This yellow warning sign tells you the number of lanes is decreasing. You need to move left.

questions.question: You missed your exit on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull over and back up to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for help.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit if you miss yours. Do not stop, back up, or make sudden lane changes on the highway. Do not cross the median. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: What must you do if a crossing guard is directing traffic in a school zone?

options.text: Follow what the crossing guard tells you.
Do what other cars are doing instead.
Assume the guard should not be there.
Follow normal rules without children present.

questions.correctAnswerText: Follow what the crossing guard tells you.
questions.explanation: Obey crossing guards, signs, and officers in school zones. Slow down and be careful when told to do so. Always drive with extra caution near schools.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with flashing lights is near you. What should you do?

options.text: Speed up to get out of the way.
Stop right away and block their path.
Clear the road and let them pass.
Signal them when it is safe to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Clear the road and let them pass.
questions.explanation: Make room for emergency vehicles with flashing lights. Pull to the side of the road when safe to give them a clear path.

questions.question: Which is unlawful?

options.text: Passing in a marked no passing zone.
Passing at a railroad crossing.
Both of the above.

questions.explanation: Do not pass in no passing zones, on hills, in curves, or where you cannot see far enough ahead. Do not pass at street crossings, railroad crossings, in work zones, or when a car stopped for a pedestrian.

questions.question: Only ____ can reduce blood alcohol content (BAC).

options.text: Drinking caffeine
Eating fatty foods
Time

questions.explanation: Only time removes alcohol and its effects from your body.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: Sudden weather changes require you to change how you drive.
You should slow down when driving in rain and fog.
Watch for vehicles coming up behind you in bad weather.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: When weather changes suddenly, adjust your driving. Always slow down in rain or fog. Watch for vehicles behind you that may be driving too fast for the conditions.

questions.question: How can you avoid becoming an aggressive driver?

options.text: Relax and focus on driving.
Drive above the posted speed limit.
Tailgate the driver in front of you.

questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, relax and focus on the road. Don't take other drivers' actions personally. Give yourself enough time to get where you're going, drive at the speed limit, and be patient with other drivers.

questions.question: How should you change lanes?

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you want to move, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, and change lanes.
Signal and change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, check your blind spot in the direction you want to move, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to see your blind spot. Make sure no one else is moving into the same lane. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: Signaling before turning, changing lanes, or leaving a curb:

options.text: Is only necessary if other traffic is around.
Is a good habit and required by law.
Is only necessary during the move, not before.
Is not necessary if you drive slowly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a good habit and required by law.
questions.explanation: Signal your intentions early when turning or changing lanes. The law requires you to signal at least 100 feet before moving your vehicle left or right. Always signal before pulling away from a curb.

questions.question: Which of these causes traffic crashes?

options.text: Speeding and driving too fast for road conditions.
Getting enough rest and staying alert.
Watching your surroundings and focusing on driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speeding and driving too fast for road conditions.
questions.explanation: Driving above the speed limit and driving too fast for conditions cause many accidents. Always drive at the speed limit and with the flow of traffic.

questions.question: Since driving has risks, it is smart to keep improving your driving and observation skills.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: Driving becomes unsafe if drivers stop trying to improve. Keep working on your driving and observation skills for your safety and the safety of others.

questions.question: What commonly causes traffic accidents?

options.text: Not paying attention while driving
Driving too fast for conditions
Following other vehicles too closely
All of the above

questions.explanation: Speeding causes many crashes. Not paying attention can lead to collisions. Most rear-end crashes happen because drivers follow too closely.

questions.question: A solid yellow arrow on a traffic light means:

options.text: Speed up to make the turn before the light changes.
You don't need to signal when turning from this lane.
Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get ready to stop and let oncoming traffic pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow arrow means the protected turn is ending. Prepare to stop and yield to oncoming traffic before turning.

questions.question: Before starting a parked car, you should:

options.text: Check the fuel gauge, adjust the radio volume, and shift gears.
Adjust the side mirror and check that your heater works.
Adjust the seat, adjust the mirrors, and fasten your seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Adjust the seat, adjust the mirrors, and fasten your seat belt.
questions.explanation: Walk around your vehicle first to check for obstacles. Before starting the engine, fasten your seat belt and adjust your seat and mirrors to safe positions.

questions.question: Drivers should keep a safe distance from cyclists.

options.text: TRUE
FALSE

questions.explanation: Drivers must be careful around cyclists and maintain a safe distance from them.

questions.question: Which is a sign of a drunk driver?

options.text: Weaving between lanes.
Driving slower than other traffic.
Making quick and sudden stops.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Signs of drunk driving include weaving, driving slowly, making jerky motions, and making quick stops.

questions.question: At a stop sign with no crosswalk, you must stop before entering the intersection.

options.text: True
False

questions.explanation: You must stop completely at the stop line. If there is no stop line, stop before the crosswalk. If there is no crosswalk, stop before entering the intersection.

questions.question: Night driving is difficult because:

options.text: The speed limit is higher at night.
There are fewer cars on the road at night.
It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is hard to judge distance and speed in the dark.
questions.explanation: Low visibility at night makes it difficult to judge distance and the speed of other vehicles. You can only see as far as your headlights allow.

questions.question: If you miss your exit on a freeway, you should:

options.text: Make a quick turn from your lane.
Stop and back up.
Continue to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.
Signal other drivers to stop so you can turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Continue to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.
questions.explanation: Do not back up on a freeway or shoulder. Instead, go to the next exit or turn where you can safely turn around.

questions.question: Driving ability can be affected by:

options.text: Alcohol.
Medication.
Lack of sleep.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Safe driving requires good physical condition. Alcohol, drugs, and drowsiness all impair your ability to drive safely.

questions.question: Check your blind spot by looking over your shoulder when:

options.text: Moving toward or away from a curb.
Turning left or right.
Changing lanes.
All of the above.

questions.explanation: Check your blind spot whenever you change your vehicle's position, including turning, changing lanes, or moving toward or away from a curb.

questions.question: When should you yield to pedestrians in a crosswalk?

options.text: Only if they wave to you first.
Only if they are not using their phone.
At all times.

questions.explanation: Always stop at a crosswalk to let pedestrians cross. You may proceed only if your lane is completely clear.

questions.question: When approaching railroad tracks, you should:

options.text: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
Speed up to cross before the gate lowers.
Try to drive around a lowered gate.
Not worry about how many tracks to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look, listen, slow down, and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Look, listen, slow down, and be prepared to stop for trains or vehicles at railroad tracks.

questions.question: If your vehicle breaks down:

options.text: Signal and move to the slow lane.
Stop in your lane and turn on hazard lights.
Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn on hazard lights and pull off the road.
questions.explanation: Get your vehicle off the road and away from traffic. Turn on your hazard lights to warn other drivers.

questions.question: A driver going much slower than the speed limit:

options.text: Is a very safe driver.
Always has the right-of-way.
Should not let cars pass.
May create a dangerous driving situation.

questions.correctAnswerText: May create a dangerous driving situation.
questions.explanation: Driving much slower than traffic flow is hazardous. On a two-lane road, pull over and let traffic pass if cars are backing up behind you. Only drive significantly under the speed limit when weather or road conditions require it.
